blocks.text: 2025 Home Color Trends
Your decisions about exterior paint are more important than you might think. You do not just apply a color; you make it fit your vision, lifestyle, local climate, neighborhood, and everything else.

blocks.text: Exterior painting sets the tone for what is inside your house and has the power to elevate it. Your home may stand out in your community or blend with it. Aesthetics aside, the paint will also protect your house for decades.

blocks.text: Earth Tones

More homeowners are gravitating toward natural, earthy tones. Shades of brown and green? People are falling in love with them! Experts say this shift results from the desire for warmth and authenticity in home design. These colors make a house look and feel lived-in, cozy, and deeply connected to its environment, which many want.

blocks.text: How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Exterior Painting

We have shared many clues to guide you in your residential exterior painting project. If you still have not landed on the perfect color, no worries. It should take a lot of back and forth! Moreover, taking your time is better than rushing into unfitting hues.
blocks.html: We have shared many clues to guide you in your residential exterior painting project. If you still have not landed on the perfect color, no worries. It should take a lot of back and forth! Moreover, taking your time is better than rushing into unfitting hues.

blocks.text: We will not leave you hanging, of course. Here are eight expert tips on how to choose the best paint colors for exterior painting.
blocks.html: We will not leave you hanging, of course. Here are eight expert tips on how to choose the best paint colors for exterior painting.

blocks.text: Look at Your Neighborhood

Walk around your neighborhood to learn its vibe. What colors are the other homes? Decide if you want to contribute to the area’s cohesive aesthetics or stand out. A good concept is to fit in but not get lost, and there is always a color to achieve that.
blocks.html: Walk around your neighborhood to learn its vibe. What colors are the other homes? Decide if you want to contribute to the area’s cohesive aesthetics or stand out. A good concept is to fit in but not get lost, and there is always a color to achieve that.

blocks.text: Observe Your Surroundings

What surrounds your house is also vital, so look at the trees, plants, and elements around you. You can paint according to your surroundings or make the surroundings work for you. If you live in a forested area, earthy tones might feel like a natural extension. In contrast, hues of the sky and sand will do well if you live in a coastal or desert community.
blocks.html: What surrounds your house is also vital, so look at the trees, plants, and elements around you. You can paint according to your surroundings or make the surroundings work for you. If you live in a forested area, earthy tones might feel like a natural extension. In contrast, hues of the sky and sand will do well if you live in a coastal or desert community.

blocks.text: Think About the Local Climate

If you live in a sunny climate, lighter colors will reflect the sun’s rays and keep your living spaces cooler. On the other hand, darker colors absorb heat, giving your house a warmer feel. Yes, your paint color will also interact with the weather, especially in terms of durability and maintenance. Factor that in, too.

blocks.text: Evaluate Your House’s Architectural Style

Traditional homes often become stunning in classic hues, while modern ones benefit from bolder choices. Does your house have historic features? You might want to stick to period-appropriate colors that preserve its charm. Generally, your exterior color improves the architectural design rather than competing with it.
blocks.html: Traditional homes often become stunning in classic hues, while modern ones benefit from bolder choices. Does your house have historic features? You might want to stick to period-appropriate colors that preserve its charm. Generally, your exterior color improves the architectural design rather than competing with it.

blocks.text: Assess Your Building Materials

Whether your house is made of brick, wood, stucco, or stone, the texture and inherent color of the building materials will affect how the coat of paint looks. For instance, red bricks pair well with creamy whites. Wooden homes, especially those with abundant natural grain, will need earthy tones or dark stains to highlight the wood’s beauty. Ask experts about this part to ensure you get a visually appealing result.

blocks.text: Consider Your Interiors

Exterior and interior design are two different worlds, but your home is a unified space. What works on the outside should flow to the inside. If you already have interior color palettes, go for exterior colors that align with them. It is possible to have varying color schemes, but they should not veer too far off, or you get a disoriented effect.

If you already have interior color palettes, go for exterior colors that align with them. It is possible to have varying color schemes, but they should not veer too far off, or you get a disoriented effect.

blocks.text: Test Swatches

Once you have a shortlist of colors, never rely on small paint chips from the store. A color might appear different when applied to the exterior versus on a sample card. Paint larger test swatches directly on the exterior of your house and see the color in various lighting throughout the day. This practice will give you the most accurate sense of how the color will work in your space.

blocks.text: Pick a Palette

Have you narrowed down your choices? Move on to a full palette of complementary shades! Exterior colors are best when layered; have a main color for the body, a trim color for architectural features, and an accent color for doors, shutters, or other focal points. Balance light and dark tones for depth and visual interest.
